case.name: Jarib

A.name: Jarib
A.line: Priest Ezra sent to Iddo (EZR 8:16), married a foreign wife (EZR 10:18)
family: descendant-of jeshua-3 (Jeshua, returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity (EZR 2:2, N)

kjv.EZR 8:16: Then sent I for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, and for Elnathan, and for Jarib, and for Elnathan, and for Nathan, and for Zechariah, and for Meshullam, chief men; also for Joiarib, and for Elnathan, men of understanding.
kjv.EZR 10:18: And among the sons of the priests there were found that had taken strange wives: namely, of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren; Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah.

B.name: Jarib
B.line: Priest, descendant of Jeshua son of Jozadak, put away his foreign wife.
family: descendant-of jeshua-3 (Jeshua, returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity (EZR 2:2, N)

kjv.EZR 10:18: And among the sons of the priests there were found that had taken strange wives: namely, of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren; Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah.

disputed_verses.BHSA EZR 10:18: וַיִּמָּצֵא֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֹשִׁ֖יבוּ נָשִׁ֣ים נָכְרִיֹּ֑ות מִבְּנֵי֙ יֵשׁ֤וּעַ בֶּן־יֹֽוצָדָק֙ וְאֶחָ֔יו מַֽעֲשֵׂיָה֙ וֶֽאֱלִיעֶ֔זֶר וְיָרִ֖יב וּגְדַלְיָֽה׃
disputed_verses.KJV EZR 10:18: And among the sons of the priests there were found that had taken strange wives: namely, of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren; Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah.

first_reader_said: EZR 10:18: Both records hold Jarib, priest of the sons of Jeshua, who had married a foreign wife.

why: Both records identify the same Jarib in EZR 10:18, a priest of the family of Jeshua son of Jozadak who married a foreign wife. B is a thinner copy of A, and A’s additional appearance among Ezra’s chief men in EZR 8:16 introduces no conflicting family, time, or role.
